'''Iván Helguera Bujía''' ({{IPA|es|iˈβan elˈɣeɾa βuˈxi.a}};<ref>In isolation, ''Bujía'' is pronounced {{IPA|es|buˈxi.a|}}</ref> born 28 March 1975) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]].

Playing as either a [[central defender]] or [[defensive midfielder]], with both good defensive and attacking skills,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/spain/squad/767898.stm|title=Ivan Helguera|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=6 June 2012}}</ref> he represented five clubs during his career, notably [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] – achieving team success as an important player – and [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]. In his early 20s, he also had an unassuming abroad spell with [[AS Roma|Roma]], going on to amass [[La Liga]] totals of 291 games and 21 goals over 11 seasons.

A [[Spain national football team|Spanish international]] on nearly 50 occasions, Helguera represented the country at the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]] and two [[UEFA European Championship|European Championships]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born and raised in [[Santander, Spain|Santander]], [[Cantabria]] and brought up at local [[Racing de Santander|Racing Club]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/noticias/deportes/tengo-clarisimo-vivire-zaragoza-algun-dia-volvere_1182149.html|title="Tengo clarísimo que viviré en Zaragoza, algún día volveré"|trans-title="It's clear as can be I will live in Zaragoza, one day I will return"|newspaper=[[El Periódico de Aragón]]|first=Ignacio|last=Martín|language=es|date=20 February 2017|access-date=23 March 2024}}</ref> Helguera started playing professionally for [[Manchego CF]] and [[Albacete Balompié]], appearing in 14 [[Segunda División]] games in the [[1996–97 Segunda División|1996–97 season]] for the latter. He was purchased by [[Serie A]] side [[AS Roma]] after that, alongside compatriot [[César Gómez]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asroma.com/en/news/2015/11/eight-spanish-stars-who-ve-played-for-roma|title=Eight Spanish stars who've played for Roma|publisher=A.S. Roma|date=17 February 2016|access-date=4 September 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180626135903/http://www.asroma.com/en/news/2015/11/eight-spanish-stars-who-ve-played-for-roma|archive-date=26 June 2018}}</ref> but left after one disappointing [[1997–98 Serie A|campaign]] to join [[RCD Espanyol]], where his stellar performances as a defender under coach [[Marcelo Bielsa]] led to a [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] deal even before [[1998–99 La Liga|1998–99]] had finished.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/1999/mayo/03/deportes/helguera.html|title=El Real Madrid ficha al espanyolista Iván Helguera por 1.200 millones de pesetas|trans-title=Real Madrid sign Espanyol man Iván Helguera for 1.200 million ''pesetas''|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=3 May 1999|access-date=26 June 2018}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
With Real Madrid from July 1999, Helguera was an instant first choice, and scored five and six [[La Liga]] goals in his [[2000–01 La Liga|second]] and [[2002–03 La Liga|fourth seasons]] (claiming the national championship on both occasions) while alternating between defender and midfielder.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://files.laliga.es/memorias/2000-2001/MemoriaLFP_2000-01.pdf|title=Memoria de La Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional {{!}} Temporada 2000/2001|trans-title=Memory of the Professional Football National League {{!}} 2000/2001 season|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://files.laliga.es/memorias/2002-2003/MemoriaLFP_2002-03.pdf|title=Memoria de La Liga de Fútbol Profesional {{!}} Temporada 2002/2003|trans-title=Memory of the Professional Football League {{!}} 2002/2003 season|publisher=La Liga|language=es|access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es-ES/noticias/futbol/primer-equipo/actualidad/goles-con-historia-helguera|title=Goles con Historia: Helguera|trans-title=Goals with History: Helguera|publisher=Real Madrid CF|language=es|date=30 September 2022|access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref> He was also instrumental in the [[Madrid|capital]] team's two victories in the [[UEFA Champions League]]: in the [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League|2000 final]], against fellow Spaniards [[Valencia CF]], he started the match as a [[Defender (association football)#Sweeper (libero)|sweeper]] in a [[2000 UEFA Champions League final|3–0 win]],<ref name=UCL1>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/may/24/championsleague.sport1|title=Real Madrid 3–0 Valencia|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=24 May 2000|access-date=3 February 2016}}</ref> appearing as stopper [[2002 UEFA Champions League final|two years later]] in the 2–1 defeat of [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]].<ref name=UCL2>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/may/15/minutebyminute.sport|title=Bayer Leverkusen 1–2 Real Madrid|newspaper=The Guardian|date=15 May 2002|access-date=26 June 2018}}</ref>

Not a starter in his final two years, Helguera still made a total of 42 appearances, scoring in a 3–1 away win over [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona]] on 28 October 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/204975?cc=5739|title=Gimnastic de Tarragona 1–3 Real Madrid|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=28 October 2006|access-date=13 June 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102233901/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/204975?cc=5739|archive-date=2 January 2013}}</ref> At the start of his [[2006–07 La Liga|last season]] he was surprisingly stripped of his No. 6 jersey which went to new signing [[Mahamadou Diarra]], given No. 21 and made to train with the youth team in anticipation of his leaving the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]], even though his contract ran until June 2009;<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD02/PUB/2006/09/02/EMD20060902028MDA.pdf|title=Otro desprecio a Helguera|trans-title=Helguera scorned again|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Óscar|last=Zárate|language=es|date=2 September 2006|access-date=20 February 2014}}</ref> however, he later managed to fight his way back into the starting eleven, being somewhat influential in helping the club to the domestic league.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cadenaser.com/articulo/deportes/Real/Madrid/gana/Liga/csrcsrpor/20070617csrcsrdep_5/Tes/|title=El Real Madrid gana su 30º título de Liga|trans-title=Real Madrid win 30th league title|publisher=[[Cadena SER]]|language=es|date=17 June 2007|access-date=23 September 2026|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110708111333/http://www.cadenaser.com/articulo/deportes/Real/Madrid/gana/Liga/csrcsrpor/20070617csrcsrdep_5/Tes/|archive-date=8 July 2011}}</ref><ref name=WBO>{{cite news|url=https://www.elespanol.com/elbernabeu/real-madrid/futbol/20200503/ivan-helguera-cantabria-champions-league-real-madrid/486231376_3.html|title=Qué fue de Iván Helguera: de Cantabria a ganar la Champions League con el Real Madrid|trans-title=What became of Iván Helguera: from Cantabria to winning the Champions League with Real Madrid|newspaper=[[El Español]]|first=Ángela|last=Castañeda|language=es|date=3 May 2020|access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

===Valencia===
On 20 July 2007, Helguera signed for Valencia on a three-year deal; upon joining, he stated that he had wanted to come for a "long time" and was "delighted" to arrive at the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2007/07/20/actualidad/1184916120_850215.html|title=El Valencia ficha a Iván Helguera hasta 2010|trans-title=Valencia sign Iván Helguera until 2010|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=20 July 2007|access-date=20 February 2014}}</ref> He was relatively important during his [[2007–08 La Liga|debut campaign]], also helping the ''Che'' to [[2007–08 Copa del Rey|win]] the [[Copa del Rey]].<ref name=Crazy>{{cite news|url=https://www.lasprovincias.es/valenciacf/frases-escribia-helguera-vestuario-desquiciar-emery-valencia-20250614224001-nt.html|title=Las frases que escribía Helguera en el vestuario para desquiciar a Emery en el Valencia: «Se volvía loco»|trans-title=The phrases Helguera wrote in the dressing room to drive Emery mad at Valencia: "He would go crazy"|newspaper=[[Las Provincias]]|first=J.|last=Zarco|language=es|date=14 June 2025|access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

However, having featured very rarely in the first part of the [[2008–09 La Liga|following season]] under [[Unai Emery]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2008/12/12/mas_futbol/1229036414_850215.html|title=Emery: "No hay nada personal entre Helguera y yo"|trans-title=Emery: "There is nothing personal between Helguera and myself"|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=12 December 2008|access-date=26 June 2018}}</ref><ref name=Crazy/> Helguera's contract was cancelled on 12 December 2008,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.valenciacf.com/contenidos/Actualidad/Noticias/2008/12/Noticia_16869.html?__locale=es|title=Rescisión de contrato de Iván Helguera|trans-title=Iván Helguera's contract termination|publisher=Valencia CF|language=es|date=12 December 2008|access-date=12 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081214230547/http://www.valenciacf.com/contenidos/Actualidad/Noticias/2008/12/Noticia_16869.html?__locale=es|archive-date=14 December 2008}}</ref> and both [[FC Dinamo București]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.prosport.ro/fotbal-intern/liga-1/un-milion-pentru-helguera-3679929|title=Un milion pentru Helguera!|trans-title=One million for Helguera!|newspaper=[[ProSport]]|first=Marius|last=Pitaru|language=ro|date=24 December 2008|access-date=24 December 2008}}</ref> and [[Los Angeles Galaxy]] declared interest in signing the player,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/13/united-states/2009/01/01/1035912/ivan-helguera-attracts-la-galaxy-interest-report|title=Ivan Helguera attracts LA Galaxy interest|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|first=Steve|last=Michaels|date=1 January 2009|access-date=1 January 2009}}</ref> but nothing came of it and he retired from football later that year.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/loc/2015/02/04/54d0f6ebca474112368b4573.html|title=Iván Helguera: 'Arrastro las lesiones que me retiraron'|trans-title=Iván Helguera: 'The injuries that retired me haunt me'|newspaper=El Mundo|first=Antonio|last=Diéguez|language=es|date=4 February 2015|access-date=26 June 2018}}</ref>

==International career==
Helguera was [[Cap (sport)|capped]] 47 times for [[Spain national football team|Spain]],<ref name=WBO/> the first coming on 18 November 1998 in an away [[Exhibition game|friendly]] with [[Italy national football team|Italy]] (2–2).<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1998/11/19/pagina-17/400568/pdf.html|title=Notable alto|trans-title=B Plus|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Javier|last=Gascón|language=es|date=19 November 1998|access-date=8 August 2013}}</ref> He played for his country at [[UEFA Euro 2000]], the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b44fc5b75-bb339e5a3edf-1000--saez-selects-spain-squad/|title=Sáez selects Spain squad|publisher=UEFA|first=Iván|last=Modia|date=20 May 2004|access-date=7 May 2016}}</ref> missing the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]] after being omitted from the squad in the months before the tournament by national team coach [[Luis Aragonés]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2006/03/30/futbol/1143744965.html|title=Helguera: "Lo mejor que me puede pasar es que venga otro entrenador"|trans-title=Helguera: "The best that can happen to me is that another manager comes"|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=30 March 2006|access-date=26 June 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Helguera's younger brother, [[Luis Helguera|Luis]], was also a professional footballer. A midfielder, he played in the first division for [[Real Zaragoza]] and [[Deportivo Alavés]], and also in Italy.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/noticias/deportes/exzaragocista-luis-helguera-apuesta-hermano-ivan_108049.html|title=El exzaragocista Luis Helguera apuesta por su hermano Iván|trans-title=Former ''zaragocista'' Luis Helguera bets on brother Iván|newspaper=El Periódico de Aragón|language=es|date=16 March 2004|access-date=7 March 2014}}</ref>

He married his longtime girlfriend Lorena, and welcomed his first baby, a boy named Luca, on 30 November 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hola.com/famosos/galeria/2004071228972/famosos/ivanhelguera/ivanhelguera/1/|title=Iván Helguera se casa en Cantabria con la periodista Lorena Casado|trans-title=Iván Helguera marries reporter Lorena Casado in Cantabria|publisher=[[¡Hola!]]|language=es|date=12 July 2004|access-date=26 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.defensacentral.com/real_madrid/48958-el-madrid-no-necesita-a-ozil|title="El Madrid no necesita a Özil"|trans-title=Madrid do not need Özil|publisher=Defensa Central|first=Gregorio|last=Revilla|language=es|date=18 August 2010|access-date=26 June 2018}}</ref>
